clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991 and within the years after: your late nights began in secondary school, you dropped chess and debate as music took over, your mother filled in your college forms while you underfunctioned, you leaned hard on Rafe at the conservatory then clashed with him once a wrist injury stopped your playing, you got high and absorbed yourself in fixing radios, and you felt lost and low with your grandfather gone and your mother about to remarry; your anxiety and functioning shifted down through these months, and your symptom rose. Your grandmother Winifred was treated for a thyroid tumour within a year or so of being widowed. Your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma in 1994. These shifts in the extended family sat beside your own troubles and are held as part of the wider disturbance.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's death, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002 and her death in February 2004: you ran out of steam for performing and felt less content by the month, you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra and were done with performing, you were on poor terms with your family and friends, you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, you met Marisol and left for Fenwick to live with her, you split within the year and sank into a deep depression, you could not face your family and your anxiety rose, you relied on friends, you returned to your therapist and your functioning began to come back up. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home. You dropped in briefly on her sickroom hung over on the way to the airport, your last visit; your anxiety rose and your relationship with her stayed at a distance. The shifts pile up through these years as you moved away from performing and from your family, the two movements side by side.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008 and within the two years after: you were drained for conversation with your mother and your relationship distanced, she pressed you to visit at Alder Creek and your anxiety rose, you kept the door shut on her when she visited, you left for nursing school in Marlow Sound and stopped speaking to your mother, a cutoff that held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation. Your partner's brother Leo's first child was born in 2010. Your shifts show a deepening distance from your mother at the same time as these changes in the extended family.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017 and within the two and a half years after: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along and your relationship moved away. Your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017. Your sister Tara married James and they live in Rennick for her work flying for a regional airline. Your aunt Imogen's memory began slipping and got worse; she lashes out when muddled and her relationship with her son Hal shifted to conflict. Your partner's brother Leo returned to Danfield with his family nearby. In October 2019, your partner was swamped one thing after another, her symptom and anxiety rose and her functioning fell; you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, and your anxiety rose; she talks with her father and brother all day in a tight fusion; once the weekend had a plan she settled. At the lake house for her mother's retirement, you awoke from the small hours with no more sleep, your symptom and anxiety rose, and you distanced yourself; your partner's anxiety rose and she felt anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions. Your own anxiety has been constantly high, you started a sleeping pill, and you began aiming for shorter, more regular calls with your mother. The shifts show a tightening around your new marriage and partnership while troubles in the extended family on both sides rose at the same time.
